claims.statement: TVI-CAMS is an internal multi-tenant compliance working layer for TVI schools running TESDA scholarship batches (TWSP/CFSP); TESDA SIS/T2MIS/BSRS remain the authoritative systems and UI copy must never imply official approval or submission (RULES rule 27).

The app is Next.js 16 App Router (next ^16.3.4, dev runs next dev --webpack), React 19.2.4, strict TypeScript, Tailwind v4, Clerk (@clerk/nextjs ^7.4.1 with ClerkProvider in the root layout), and pnpm (packageManager pnpm@9.15.4).
Node 22+ is hard-required: Vitest 4's rolldown calls util.styleText with an array argument that throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE on Node 21 or older, before any test loads.

The app talks directly to one hosted Supabase project (Postgres + Storage) with no separate backend and no staging environment; Express.js (Node/TypeScript) is documented as a future-only backend direction that must not be built or treated as present.

proxy.ts (repo root) is the Clerk middleware whose matcher covers every non-static route plus __clerk and api/trpc; it stamps an x-pathname header for Server Components and does not itself force authentication.

Route protection happens in app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx, which calls requireAuthenticatedUser() from modules/auth/data/auth.ts and redirects anonymous visitors to /sign-in; app/page.tsx is a bare 307 redirect to /dashboard.

The dashboard layout resolves identity before rendering: one profile snapshot feeds the trusted role (resolveTrustedRole, never the ?role= preview override), the ADR-006 platform-admin axis (isPlatformAdmin), and the tenant-access fold (withTenantAccess) over the batches snapshot, which is React cache()-wrapped so the layout and its nested page share one Supabase query per request.

The server-side Supabase client is built with the anon key and an accessToken callback that returns the Clerk session token; a missing token throws NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE rather than silently querying as anon, because RLS against anon returns zero rows with no error — the dangerous outcome for a compliance tool.

Postgres RLS (app_private.* helper functions from the canonical migration, reading only sub from the JWT) makes every authorization decision — RLS is the security boundary and UI hiding is usability only (RULES rule 1); the app uses Clerk's native third-party auth integration because Supabase JWT templates were deprecated 1 Apr 2025 and the schema needs no custom claims.

The service-role client (lib/supabase/service.ts) bypasses RLS and is confined to the Clerk webhook provisioning path — modules/auth/data/provisioning.ts, invoked only from app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (creates profiles on user.created, deactivates on user.deleted) — and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must never be NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed or read outside that file.
Import direction app → modules → shared → lib/supabase is lint-enforced by import/no-restricted-paths zones in eslint.config.mjs (RULES rule 7, [lint]).

lib/supabase/database.types.ts (generated raw DB row types) may be imported only from module data/ layers and lib/supabase itself — not from app/, shared/, or any module domain/ or ui/ code; components import domain types from shared/types.ts only (RULES rule 10, [lint]).

ESLint zones forbid shared/ from importing modules/ or app/, forbid modules/ from importing app/, and make each of the 14 modules' data/ private to itself (zones generated from the domains array) while app/ may fetch from any module's data/ (RULES rules 8-9, [lint]).

modules/ holds exactly 14 domain modules — one per PRD FR (auth FR-01 through reports FR-15) plus shell for app chrome — the same set named in the ESLint domains array; new code goes inside its owning module, never in a new top-level folder (RULES rule 12).

modules/tenancy now has ui/ (CreateUserForm.tsx, CreateSchoolForm.tsx) in addition to data/ and domain/: user administration (role and membership writes through the Clerk-scoped anon client so RLS decides) and the ADR-006 school registry (create_school RPC, platform-admin check), with pure draft rules in domain/userAccess.ts and domain/schoolDraft.ts.

Platform admin (ADR-006) is a separate axis from profile_role — resolved via a security definer RPC (isPlatformAdmin in modules/tenancy/data/platform.ts) because public.platform_admins is deliberately unreadable through the anon client — and its reach is the school registry only; granting it any compliance table or letting it seat itself into a tenant is a boundary change needing its own ADR (RULES rule 30).

modules/attendance/, modules/lamr/, and modules/notifications/ are README-only stubs with no code: attendance plans data/attendance.ts + domain/eligibility.ts (the ≥5-absences rule) against the planned attendance_records table, lamr plans LAMR report fetch/map and evidence UI, and notifications remains unimplemented while alerts are computed on read (the dashboard AlertsPanel still lives in modules/batches/ui/dashboard/).

Where RULES.md and CLAUDE.md appear to disagree, RULES.md wins and the drift should be fixed; below the rules, docs precedence is docs/MASTER_PRD_SRS.md → docs/TRD.md → docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, with the ADRs in docs/adr/ overriding or amending those documents (RULES rules 30-31).

The operative ADR chain is ADR-001 (billing is a document-generating engine; supersedes any 'billing = preparation signal only' wording) → ADR-003 (amends ADR-001 §4: the packet queue is a projection of (batch, billing_type, tranche) with the draft → ready → generated → submitted → settled lifecycle, derived due dates, and user-asserted submitted/settled marks) → ADR-006 (supersedes PRD FR-02's 'Super Admin is not implemented' with a platform admin that provisions the school registry only).

The ≥5-absences ineligibility rule (stored as max_absences = 4) remains a locked domain fact in RULES.md and CONTEXT.md — no ADR supersedes it — alongside progress = sessions_held / total_sessions (nominal hours ÷ 8, snapshotted on the batch), one RQM code = one batch, ULI as the permanent learner key, tenant context in the URL path segment, alerts computed on read (no cron/email), billing as the document-generating engine, and the ADR-003 packet lifecycle.
RULES rule 34 ('no test runner yet — pnpm test is a placeholder') is known drift predating the Vitest stand-up: pnpm test now runs vitest run with 21 unit spec files in tests/unit/.

assets/, preview/, screenshots/, ui_kits/, and uploads/ are ported verbatim from the design bundle: excluded from lint via globalIgnores in eslint.config.mjs, and edit-blocked by the PreToolUse hook .claude/hooks/protect-static-dirs.sh (RULES rule 28, [hook]) which explicitly carves out public/assets/ (the app's real runtime static directory); FIGMA FILES/, diagrams/, and .design-sync/ are review-level design artifacts, not app code (RULES rule 29).

pnpm dev runs next dev --webpack, pnpm build/start build and serve, pnpm lint runs the flat ESLint config, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit strict-typechecks (no dedicated script), pnpm test runs Vitest, pnpm test:e2e runs Playwright with a pnpm-dev web server on :3000, and pnpm preview serves the static design bundle on :5000.

Unit tests cover mappers and pure module domain/ layers with fixed as-of dates; the Playwright spec exercises unauthenticated access to a dashboard route being redirected to /sign-in (the layout gate, not proxy.ts); real-Supabase RLS/tenant-isolation integration tests are still outstanding and must run against the real hosted project with no mocks (RULES rule 35).

supabase/migrations/ holds seven SQL files — 20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql is canonical for schema + RLS and the latest, 20260910120000_add_adr001_billing_domain.sql (the ADR-001 billing domain), is pending; dev seed data now lives in supabase/seeds/, not migrations/; the live schema is 18 tables / 36 foreign keys / seven database enums.
